findings.evidence: "Check the message again and enter all six."
findings.fix: Name the source explicitly, e.g., "Check the code we sent you and enter all six digits."
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - first message (wrong digit count)
findings.violation: "The message" is ambiguous - it could mean the on-screen error text being read right now or the external SMS/email that contains the actual code, so the instruction doesn't clearly tell the user where to look.

findings.evidence: Predictable mistake: yes / Suggested fix: none
findings.fix: Suggest a prevention mechanism, e.g., "input mask limiting entry to 6 digits," rather than leaving "Suggested fix" as none.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - first message (wrong digit count)
findings.violation: A predictable mistake like an incomplete code is normally one the form should prevent outright (e.g., by limiting input to six digits), yet no preventive fix is suggested here - the entry only catches the error after the fact.

findings.fix: Clear the field when this error fires (or when a new code is sent), reserving "preserved" for errors the user can actually correct by editing.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - second message (expired code)
findings.violation: The entered code is permanently invalid once expired - editing it can't fix it - so preserving it in the field risks the user resubmitting the same dead code instead of the newly sent one.

findings.fix: Include the year, e.g., "This promo code ended on 30 June 2026."
findings.location: Billing, promo code - first message (expired code)
findings.violation: The date omits the year, so it's unclear whether the code expired this year, last year, or some other time - ambiguous for a message that's specifically about timing.

findings.evidence: Promo message: "Fires: on-blur"; 2FA expired message: "Fires: on-submit"
findings.fix: Fire both on the same event (e.g., on-blur for both), or add a stated reason why the verification code must wait until submission while the promo code does not.
findings.location: Billing, promo code - first message (expired code), compared to Two-factor setup second message
findings.violation: Both messages validate the same kind of condition - a code that has gone stale relative to server-held data - yet they fire at different points in the interaction with no explanation, making the triggering logic inconsistent between otherwise-parallel cases.

findings.evidence: Promo message: "Suggested fix: none"; 2FA expired message: "Suggested fix: selectable, offers a resend code button in place of the message"
findings.fix: Apply the same pattern to the promo message, e.g., add a "browse current codes" or "remove code" button in place of plain text.
findings.location: Billing, promo code - first message (expired code), compared to Two-factor setup second message
findings.violation: Both are time-expired, unfixable-by-editing conditions, but only one gets an actionable remediation (a button); the promo message gets no equivalent suggestion despite being equally suited to one.

findings.evidence: Plan-mismatch message: "Predictable mistake: yes"; expired-code message: "Predictable mistake: no"
findings.fix: Align the two - either mark both predictable (since the rules are known server-side in advance) or explain why expiry differs from plan-restriction in this respect.
findings.location: Billing, promo code - second message (plan mismatch), compared to first message (expired code)
findings.violation: Both conditions depend on server-known metadata about the promo code (its plan restriction vs. its expiry date) that is equally knowable ahead of submission, so labeling one predictable and the other not applies the predictability criterion inconsistently.

findings.evidence: Predictable mistake: yes / Suggested fix: none
findings.fix: Propose a prevention mechanism in "Suggested fix," such as disabling the promo code field when the selected plan is incompatible with it.
findings.location: Billing, promo code - second message (plan mismatch)
findings.violation: As with the digit-count message, a predictable mismatch should normally prompt a preventive fix (e.g., disabling or hiding the promo field for incompatible plans), but none is suggested.

findings.evidence: "Signal: bold text set larger than the field label, icon" repeated identically in every entry
findings.fix: Scale the signal to severity - reserve bold/larger text plus icon for higher-stakes messages and use a lighter inline treatment for simple correctable format errors.
findings.violation: The same high-intensity visual treatment is used for a minor format error (wrong digit count) and a security-relevant message (expired 2FA code), failing to differentiate severity and risking alert fatigue or mismatched urgency.
